subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The Greek Debt Crisis
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Greek Debt Crisis usable.

hook.text: Greece borrowed too much, lied about its deficit, and nearly destroyed the entire eurozone in the process.

buildup.text: By 2010, Greece's debt reached 146% of GDP. Markets realized it couldn't repay and interest rates exploded.

discovery.text: The EU and IMF imposed severe austerity in exchange for bailout loans. Greece's economy shrank by 25%.

twist.text: Greece's crisis spread contagion fears to Italy, Spain, and Portugal, threatening the euro's very existence.

climax.text: The Greek crisis showed that one country's debt problem can threaten an entire monetary union.

punchline.text: Borrowed too much. Economy shrank 25%. Nearly broke the euro.

quiz.question: What broader impact did the Greek debt crisis have?
options: It threatened the entire eurozone through contagion fears
